chain.g: exclamation of surprise, grief, or joy

ety.text: Inherited from Middle English lo, loo, from Old English lā (“exclamation of surprise, grief, or joy”). Conflated in Middle English with lo! (interjection), a corruption of lok!, loke! (“look!”) (as in lo we! (look we!)). Cognate with Scots lo, lu (“lo”). See also look.
Borrowed from Hokkien 囉 /啰 (--lo͘). Doublet of lor.

senses.d: look, see, behold (in an imperative sense).
ex: Caliban: Lo, lo again! Bite him to death, I prithee.
[...], Lo, these many years do I serve thee, [...].

senses.d: Sentence-final particle denoting finality or completion.

ety.text: Literally, “look here”. From vois (“see!, look!”), second-person singular imperative of voir (“to see, to look”) and ci (“here”).
Literally, “look there”. From vois (“see!, look!”), second-person singular imperative of voir (“to see, to look”) and là (“there”).

it:ecco.gl: here it is! there you have it!

chain.g: there or here I am/you are/he is; here I come/you come/he comes; here is, see here

ety.text: Inherited from Latin eccum, from ecce + eum.
